title: Branches under a compiler
subtitle: Watch two if-statements become compares and jumps.
intro: Three lines of C, each a branch. Step by source line to watch control flow, then step by instruction to see each CMP set the flags a Jcc reads. The sign of x decides the first branch; the zero test decides the second.

title: A loop, instruction by instruction
subtitle: One C for-loop; count the back-edges.
intro: The accumulator lives in a register; the loop counter is compared each turn. Step by line to ride the loop, or by instruction to see the increment, the compare, and the conditional back-edge that the C for-header hides.

title: Recursion on the real stack
subtitle: Step into a call; finish out of it.
intro: Each call pushes a return address and a frame. Use Step line to descend into fib(n-1), Finish to run a call to its return, and the stack view to watch the frames pile up and unwind.

title: A global the function writes
subtitle: Watch a static array change in memory.
intro: The table is a static array in .bss, loaded writable at 0x2000. Open the Memory tab and step: the first loop zeroes the table, then each octal digit of x bumps a counter, so you see the array fill byte by byte. The return value is the largest count. For 511 (0o777) that is three.

title: Floating point in the XMM registers
subtitle: Integers in, a double computed, an integer out.
intro: Floating point lives in the XMM registers, not the general-purpose ones. The integers are converted with cvtsi2sd, summed and divided with addsd/divsd, then truncated back with cvttsd2si. Watch xmm0 in the Registers tab hold the running double. For 10, 20, 33 the mean is 21.
